title: The Midnight Choir
premise: Dominic Oyelaran has spent his life as the crown's food-taster, swallowing poison in measured doses to build immunity, safe inside a valley where magic cannot follow. When the king declares a hunt for all gifted souls, Dominic learns his late sister's spirit was sold to the court beneath the mountain to pay his own debts, and that her soul will be consumed at the solstice feast. Breaking his oath of invisibility, he descends with a disgraced choir-mistress who once sang the dead across thresholds, trading his immunity—his one protection—for passage through poisoned halls. In the end, Dominic must choose between exposing the court's crimes and losing his sister forever; he sings her name into the royal ledger, shattering the valley's spell, and justice arrives not by law but by every stolen soul remembering itself at once.
about_author: Silas Okafor is a former archivist from the river towns who spent a decade cataloguing funeral songs before turning to fiction. He writes about ordinary people caught between institutions and the things institutions bury.

chapters.title: The Taster's Oath
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. We meet him mid-service, tasting the king's soup, cataloguing poisons like prayers, and keeping his head down in the magic-dead valley. A routine meal nearly kills him—a new toxin—and he realizes someone at court wants him dead specifically. Emotional beat: uneasy belonging; he loves the palace that would erase him.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The crown announces a hunt for the gifted; neighbors begin informing on neighbors. That night Dominic finds his mother's old letters revealing his sister Adaeze's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain to settle his apprenticeship debt. Emotional beat: guilt detonating into purpose—the hunt makes hiding meaningless anyway.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Sang Doors
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, then shifting to Nneka the choir-mistress. He seeks out Nneka, exiled for singing a nobleman's dead son back too far, and bargains: his body's immunity to poison can carry them through the mountain's toxic breath if she teaches him the threshold songs. Emotional beat: two broken oaths recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Leaving the Valley
chapters.summary: Nneka's POV. Crossing the valley's edge is agony—magic floods back into Dominic like drowning, and the immunity he built begins burning off with every league. They evade the first hunter-wardens using a funeral procession as cover. Emotional beat: grief for the safety he chose never to feel safe in.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the road they shelter a gifted child hunted by wardens, forcing a choice: speed or mercy. They take the child, losing their lead, and gain an unexpected ally who knows the mountain's servant tunnels. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh—every kindness costs time Adaeze doesn't have.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They enter the court beneath the mountain, where the nobility are half-consumed by the souls they've eaten and music is currency. Dominic poses as a taster sent ahead for the solstice feast. He glimpses Adaeze—not saved, but serving, her memory already fraying. Emotional beat: horror wearing hospitality's face.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Nneka's POV. Nneka infiltrates the archive where sold souls are recorded and discovers the king himself brokered the trade—and that Dominic's immunity was engineered to make him a vessel for the feast's final course. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed; the law was never neutral, only hungry.

chapters.title: What the Poison Remembers
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Captured after Adaeze fails to recognize him, Dominic is prepared as the feast's vessel. In the cells he meets the half-eaten souls and realizes his immunity isn't armor—it's a ledger of every poison, and poisons remember their makers. Emotional beat: despair transmuting into terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Midnight Choir
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. At the solstice feast, Nneka leads the stolen souls in song while Dominic drinks the court's ceremonial cup willingly, letting every poison name its maker aloud. The king's crimes ring through the mountain; the court devours itself as the souls reclaim their names. Emotional beat: catharsis—justice sung, not sentenced.

chapters.title: Morning Over the Valley
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, resolution. The valley's spell is broken; magic and memory return together. Adaeze, restored but changed, chooses to cross onward rather than stay, and Dominic lets her go with a full goodbye. He returns not to serve but to testify, rebuilding the choir with Nneka. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace—truth outliving both loyalty and law.
